_doc: Activity feed golden cases (docs/API.md 'Feed'). cases: apply events (the group's whole log, seq 1 is group.created) in order and build an ActivityItem for each event from the states just before and just after it; expected is the result after the hiding rules, newest first, and texts (same order) are the English sentences as seen by the viewer me. expected leaves out null keys and empty changes (compared as if absent). groupId and feedId are DB values, so they aren't here. actorMemberId is the member linked to actorUserId in the state just after, else looked up in the state after the whole log. The server checks items and texts, the app checks expected→texts (the formatter). batches: server push batch sentences (the app doesn't use them). money: money notation (shared/currencies.json symbols). Phase 3: when there is exactly one payer both before and after, changes has no payers (they followed amount and paidBy by rule 10), and when either side has several payers, changes has no paidBy (it is derived from payers, so ties and small edits flip it). A refund's expense_added has refund: true. Phase 4: a currency not in symbols (a new currency) has its ISO code as the prefix (ZAR1,234.56, OMR1,234.567, XOF1,500). Phase 5: a category change uses the names the app shows (labelOf: the label, *.other as 'Entertainment - Other', null and legacy as General): 'category General → Dining out', and just 'category' when both sides are the same. Phase 6: in a friend group (kind "friend" in the seq 1 group.created) seq 1 and 2 are hidden, and any other member.added is friend_added ("{A} added {member} as a friend"). expense.deleted with movedTo is expense_moved (the same fields as expense_deleted, "{A} moved “{description}” to another group"). comment_added with a paymentId fills the payment's fields at the time of the comment (paymentId, fromMember, toMember, amount, currency) plus commentId and text, with expenseId and description null ("{A} commented on a payment of {M(amount)} from {from} to {to}: {text}"). A payment edit (payment_deleted + payment_added) batches as "{A} made 2 changes". Phase 7: attachment.added is receipt_added, attachment.deleted is receipt_removed (expenseId and description = the just-after values of the expense the receipt is on, "{A} added a receipt to “{description}”" / "{A} removed a receipt from “{description}”"). attachment.added of an id already there and attachment.deleted of an already deleted receipt are hidden (hiding rule 1). payment.restored is payment_restored (the same fields as payment_added, "{A} restored a payment of {M(amount)} from {from} to {to}"); restored on a live payment or on one replaced by an edit is hidden (hiding rule 1). payment.deleted with a string replacedBy (a payment edit) is payment_edited, not payment_deleted (the same fields, the old payment's values, "{A} edited a payment of {M(amount)} from {from} to {to}"). A payment edit (payment_edited + payment_added) still batches as "{A} made 2 changes". batches: of the items sent as a visible notification, a receipt_added whose batch has an expense_added with the same expenseId is dropped first (if one item is left, its sentence). Phase 8 (recurring expenses): recurrence.created → recurrence_created, recurrence.updated → recurrence_updated, recurrence.deleted → recurrence_deleted. All three fill recurrenceId, frequency and the description, amount and currency of the template just after (no myDelta). recurrence_updated's changes read the templates just before and just after as expenses (applied like expense.created) and follow the same rules and order as expense_updated (a template has no date). recurrence.created of an id already there, and recurrence.updated or recurrence.deleted of an unknown or stopped series, are hidden (hiding rule 1). expense.created with a null actorUserId and a recurrenceId (a repeat made by the server scheduler) is expense_repeated: the fields of expense_added + frequency, no actorMemberId. expense_* items fill recurrenceId when the expense just after is in a series. expense_updated and recurrence_updated with empty changes (for example an edit that changed only the series tags recurrenceId and occurrence) are hidden (hiding rule 7). Sentences: "{A} set “{description}” to repeat {frequency}", "{A} changed future “{description}”: {changes}", "{A} stopped “{description}” repeating", "“{description}” · {M(amount)} was added (repeats {frequency})" + the same tail as expense_added (for a refund "A refund “…” · … was added (repeats …)" and you get back). Frequency words: weekly / every 2 weeks / monthly / yearly. batches: a recurrence_* item whose batch has an expense_* item with the same recurrenceId is dropped first (making a repeating expense, changing it and future repeats, and deleting it and stopping the series read as the expense's one sentence). When all are expense_repeated: "{n} repeating expenses were added" (no Someone even without an actor). Phase 9 (languages, docs/API.md 'Languages and web'): sentences are built from the language blocks of shared/strings.json. cases, batches and money without lang are en, and the English sentences are byte-for-byte the same as before Phase 9. A money[] lang (en when missing) is a strings.json language and the notation is M(x) (docs/API.md 'Money notation'). Phase 9 changed 6 English goldens: when a symbol ends in a Latin letter and the pattern is {s}{n}, a U+00A0 goes between them (CHF unchanged; SEK and KWD left the symbol table and use the ISO code; ZAR, OMR and XOF were ISO codes already). localized: per-language goldens (part of the translation review). The same shape as batches plus lang: one item gives its sentence (app and server), two or more give the push batch sentence (server only, the same rules as batches); with remind, instead of items there is {from: the sender's name, amounts: [{currency, amount}]}, and title and text are the reminder push (server only). A lang not in strings.json is built as en. Phase 10: group.deleted → group_deleted, group.restored → group_restored (name = the group's name just after; a second delete on the same state is hidden, hiding rule 1), and group_updated's changes gain type (from and to as sent; the sentence is 'type {to}' with words.groupType, an unknown value reads Other) and coverImageId (no value, 'cover photo'). In a friend group (seq 1 kind "friend") the group_deleted and group_restored sentences are activity.friend_deleted and friend_restored ("{A} deleted your non-group expenses") instead of the internal group name.
